notes: ci.yml's macros-tests job runs `scripts/test.sh --filter ToolSchemaMacro --traits Macros --skip-update` per-PR whenever Sources/ManifoldMacrosPlugin/**, Sources/ManifoldInference/Macros/**, or Tests/ManifoldInferenceTests/ToolSchemaMacro*.swift change (ci.yml's macros filter); ToolSchemaMacroIntegrationTests.swift applies @ToolSchema to WeatherArgs/WeatherUnits, builds a ToolDefinition from the synthesised .jsonSchema, and round-trips a TypedToolExecutor dispatch through real JSON encode/decode -- a compiled, executed proof of the AGENTS.md @ToolSchema recipe (which is itself a no-build doc snippet); ToolSchemaMacroTests.swift covers the pure syntax-expansion surface (assertMacroExpansion) in the same job/filter but is deliberately NOT this row's vehicle -- it never dispatches through a real ToolDefinition/executor, so it doesn't demonstrate end-to-end usage the way the integration suite does. lane_methods names all three real methods in the vehicle file (testSynthesisedSchemaShape, testRoundTripThroughTypedToolExecutor, testOptionalFieldCanBeOmitted); resolved via lane_ref's own bare .swift path, not the Example/AdvancedUITests default -- demo-coverage.sh's lane_methods resolution was generalized in this PR (resolve_lane_method_suite_file) specifically so a Tests/**-rooted vehicle can be method-bound. ci.yml's `--filter ToolSchemaMacro` is a substring match against ToolSchemaMacroIntegrationTests, so the same lane_ref workflow entry reaches all three named methods. Coverage gap worth recording: ci.yml's macros paths filter covers Sources/ManifoldMacrosPlugin/**, Sources/ManifoldInference/Macros/**, and the ToolSchemaMacro*.swift test files, but NOT the code the vehicle actually dispatches through -- Sources/ManifoldContract/ToolExecutor.swift (TypedToolExecutor) and Sources/ManifoldInference/Services/ToolSchemaEncoder.swift live outside that filter, so a regression there doesn't select the macros-tests job. It's also not caught by the standard test job as a fallback: all three of that job's XCTest/Swift Testing invocations build with no trait flags (ci.yml's own comment on this), and ToolSchemaMacroIntegrationTests.swift is wrapped in `#if Macros`, so it compiles out entirely there. The only per-PR lane is the path-filtered macros-tests job; nightly-slow-tests.yml's queue-merge-backstop job is the <=24h fallback when the filter misses a change, per AGENTS.md's Documentation gates section on satellite jobs. This is also the manifest's only `per-pr` row -- every other executed row is weekly/manual/external/live-e2e/release-gate.

title: manifold-server executable (Server trait)
notes: M3; scripts/example-server.sh boots the REAL compiled manifold-server binary (Server-trait build), curls /health and auth-gated /v1/models for route/envelope/auth coverage, and separately curls /v1/chat/completions against a live Ollama backend — the gap the existing per-PR suite doesn't close, since Tests/ManifoldServerTests (ManifoldServerSmokeTests + siblings, 136 tests, verified 2026-08-09) drives ServerApp's routing/adapter logic only through HummingbirdTesting's in-process app.test(.router) client with a FakeBackendProvider/FixedChatAdapter — never the compiled binary listening on a real socket. Narrowed claim (external review): only /v1/chat/completions is real-backend evidence. TraitAwareServerBackendProvider.listModels() never contacts Ollama for the ollama selection — it echoes back the --model flag this script itself passed in — so GET /v1/models proves the route, response envelope, and auth enforcement (paired with the 401 check on the unauthenticated call), not that Ollama was reached; only the chat-completions call round-trips through backend(for:) into a real generation. Declared lane is per-pr (not manual) because that suite already fires on Sources/ManifoldServer*/** + Tests/ManifoldServerTests/** changes via ci.yml's server-tests job (scripts/test.sh --filter ManifoldServerTests --traits Server) — real request/response assertions, scripted/mock backend, path-gated the same way every other suite in this repo is. The script itself is not wired into any CI lane; it is the stronger live-backend, live-process vehicle a human runs by hand (scripts/example-server.sh all). lane_methods left empty — a deliberate decision, re-examined after #2465, not an inheritance of the old excuse. lane_ref names a directory (Tests/ManifoldServerTests, 17 sibling suite files, 136 tests), not a bare .swift path, so the requirement still doesn't trigger; but I tried binding it anyway to check whether it SHOULD, by pointing lane_ref at one real file (Tests/ManifoldServerTests/ManifoldServerSmokeTests.swift) and naming two of its real methods (testRoutesReturnHealthModelsAndChatCompletion, testBearerAuthProtectsAPIButExemptsHealthOnly). Two findings from that attempt, both real: (1) demo-coverage.sh --check rejects it — confirmed empirically against a fixture using the verbatim ci.yml line. #2465's workflow-linkage check only tests whether the --filter value is a substring of 'Suite/method' (e.g. 'ManifoldServerSmokeTests/testFoo'); it never considers the enclosing SPM TEST TARGET name, which is what --filter ManifoldServerTests actually matches here (ManifoldServerTests is the target in Package.swift, not a class — swift test's real match key is 'TargetName.ClassName/method', and 'ManifoldServerTests' is NOT a substring of 'ManifoldServerSmokeTests/testFoo' the way the check currently constructs it, even though the real filter genuinely does select these tests). This is a real gap in #2465's already-merged logic, not a reason specific to this row — flagging it under #2453 for a follow-up rather than patching demo-coverage.sh again inside this PR, which is scoped to the server vehicle. (2) Independent of that bug: --filter ManifoldServerTests is target-scoped, so ci.yml's server-tests job runs ALL 136 tests across all 17 files whenever it fires, never a subset. Naming 2-4 methods here (matching every other populated lane_methods row's size) would misrepresent a whole-target execution as if only those methods were checked, understating real coverage rather than the overclaiming lane_methods exists to catch — a second, independent reason this row's execution is genuinely suite-level, not method-level, even once the tooling gap above is fixed.
